title: Grain Marketing Contracts: Checkoff, Capital Retain and Patronage Eligibility by Programme
content:
Two withholdings and one entitlement are catalogued against the marketing programmes of Grain Marketing Contracts: the statutory commodity checkoff, the per-unit capital retain, and whether bushels marketed under the programme earn a patronage allocation at all.

| Programme | Checkoff withheld on settled bushels (USD per bushel) | Days a member has to ask the checkoff back | Per-unit capital retain (USD per bushel) | Bushels earn patronage allocation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spot Cash Delivery Ticket | 0.0075 | 45 | 0.000 | No |
| Forward Cash Sale Contract | 0.0075 | 45 | 0.003 | Yes |
| Basis Fixed Contract | 0.0075 | 45 | 0.003 | Yes |
| Hedge-to-Arrive Contract | 0.0075 | 45 | 0.003 | Yes |
| Delayed Price Agreement | 0.0075 | 45 | 0.003 | Yes |
| Minimum Price Contract | 0.0075 | 45 | 0.003 | Yes |
| Managed Accumulator Program | 0.0075 | 45 | 0.003 | Yes |

The checkoff rate and the refund window stand at the same figures on every marketing programme. The capital retain and the patronage entitlement move together: the Spot Cash Delivery Ticket is the one programme in the catalogue marked as earning no patronage allocation, and it is also the one programme carrying no per-unit retain.

## Illustration on hypothetical bushels

On a hypothetical settlement of 10,000 bushels drawn on a Hedge-to-Arrive Contract, the checkoff withheld is 75.00, being 0.0075 per bushel on those bushels, and the per-unit capital retain withheld is 30.00, being 0.003 per bushel. The same 10,000 bushels on a Spot Cash Delivery Ticket carry the same 75.00 of checkoff and no retain at all.
